The Android app does not currently support folders creation.

If your account connects via Imap, a workaround is to create folders using your webmail. They will then sync to the mobile app. Thereafter you can move emails to and from these folders within the app.

content:
Having only an outbox displayed occurs when the account's sign-in didn't complete successfully during setup or import. This can happen if the Oauth 2.0 account sign-in process was skipped or an unsupported configuration was imported.

Are the accounts using ...

  1. Imap or pop3 connections?
  2. What authentication type is used on each. Oauth 2.0 or user name & password.

For the two accounts, can you navigate to

  1. Settings > account > fetching mail > incoming server.
  2. Settings > account > Sending mail > outgoing server.

Click next on both screens to establish and test the server connection.

Port 993 = Imap, Port 995 = Pop3 on the incoming server page.

For oAuth authentication, you might be prompted to sign-in to your provider and grant the app permission to access your email account. Click the "sign-in with google" button as example.

Note that Thunderbird for Android doesn't support using OAuth with Pop3 connections. If this is the issue, you will need to create an app password via your webmail setting.

content:
The app normally displays pages using webview. Do you have the 'Android system webview' app installed and up to date?

It's also possible that Brave is set as the default handler for web links. You could try clearing Brave as the default link handlers (if set) and see if that helps. Opening links will then display a popup asking which browser to use or set as default.

  1. Goto android settings > apps > Brave
  2. Tap open by default
  3. Clear default

The location of the setting may be slightly different depending on Android version and phone manufacturer.
